paper_metadata.title: ML-Driven Quantum Portfolio Optimization: Hybrid CNN-LSTM Architecture with Adaptive Zero-Noise Extrapolation on NISQ Devices

summary: The paper studies QAOA-based portfolio optimization on a 6-qubit benchmark using a Qiskit Aer density-matrix simulator with the FakeMontreal noise model, and reports that ML-ZNE reduces extrapolation error by 58% relative to static ZNE. It also reports portfolio-performance improvements, including a 16.8% Sharpe-ratio improvement over static ZNE and 9.2% under market volatility, but does not show a classical speedup or quantum advantage over classical solvers.

experiments.description: QAOA-based quantum portfolio optimization evaluated under static ZNE and ML-driven ZNE using a hybrid CNN-LSTM noise predictor on a 6-qubit benchmark circuit and portfolio instances derived from Fama-French data.

algorithm.variant: QAOA with depth 4 and ML-ZNE error mitigation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Portfolio selection encoded as an Ising/QUBO-style binary selection problem with xi in {0,1} representing asset inclusion; QAOA used to estimate expectation values of the cost Hamiltonian.
problem_formulation.objective_function: H = sum_i mu_i x_i - gamma * sum_{i,j} x_i x_j (as written in the paper; portfolio performance evaluated via Sharpe ratio from estimated expectation values)
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H = sum_i mu_i x_i - gamma * sum_{i,j} x_i x_j

problem_instance.description: Quantum portfolio optimization on a 5-asset/6-qubit benchmark setting, with additional scalability tests across circuit depths; financial performance evaluated on Fama-French factors and portfolios.

dataset_specification.description: Daily market returns from 1990-02-07 to 2025-10-31; normalized returns used to compute baseline and Sharpe ratios.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Returns normalized; synthetic quantum calibration data constructed by adding small Gaussian perturbations over 10 time steps to a 27x5 feature matrix; portfolio instances built from historical returns and covariances.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison of ML-ZNE vs static ZNE and unmitigated optimization using mean absolute error for expectation values and Sharpe ratio for portfolio performance; scalability assessed across circuit depths 1, 2, 4, and 6.

noise_model.noise_type: decoherence, gate errors, measurement/readout error, calibration drift
noise_model.error_mitigation_method: zero-noise extrapolation with ML-based adaptive extrapolation (CNN-LSTM) and static polynomial ZNE baseline
noise_model.mitigation_details: Noise scaling via simplified circuit repetition and standard unitary folding; static ZNE used second-order polynomial fitting; ML-ZNE trained on noisy/ideal expectation pairs with calibration features.

implementation_details.transpilation_target: IBM Quantum backend noise model (FakeMontreal) via Qiskit Aer density-matrix simulation
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Calibration data transformed into 27x5 qubit feature vectors; temporal drift simulated with Gaussian perturbations over 10 time steps; financial returns normalized.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Expectation values converted to Sharpe ratio for portfolio performance comparison; absolute error and deviation metrics computed.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports error-mitigation and portfolio-performance improvements, but no computational speedup, asymptotic advantage, or runtime reduction over a classical baseline.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; experiments are on a 6-qubit benchmark with depth sweeps over 1, 2, 4, 6
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require a fault-tolerant or substantially larger NISQ/QPU implementation plus evidence of scaling beyond toy portfolio instances; current study only shows mitigation improvements on a simulator with hardware noise model
limiting_factors: No runtime or asymptotic speedup is reported
Only a 6-qubit benchmark circuit is used
Performance gains are relative to static ZNE and unmitigated optimization, not classical portfolio solvers
The work relies on noisy simulation with FakeMontreal rather than a real QPU
Classical COBYLA is used for optimization

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_noisy because the paper states a density-matrix simulation in Qiskit Aer using the FakeMontreal backend noise model rather than a real QPU.
